user_message: A disease affects 1 in 1,000 people. A test detects 99% of cases and falsely tests positive for 1% of healthy people. If someone tests positive, roughly how likely are they to have the disease?
allowed_evidence: For a population of 100,000, expected counts may be used to apply Bayes' rule. Sensitivity is P(positive|disease); false-positive rate is P(positive|no disease).
public_rubric: Computes the posterior probability correctly to a sensible precision.
Uses concrete expected counts or an equivalent Bayes calculation.
Explains why the result differs from 99%.
